events.text:
## Summary

**Specification submitted:** Single feature **#13, long** (weight +1, no combination needed)

**Process:**
1. Declared three stopping rules upfront (best_so_far_above 1.2, failures_at_least 2, last_gain_at_most 0.05) — all as "stop" actions.
2. Used my one allowed `pick_prior`-eligible slot by skipping it (no non-data-driven conviction here) and went straight to `init`, which anchors on the single best feature out of all 80 (40 features × 2 signs).
3. `init` immediately returned feature 13 (long) with an in-sample annualized Sharpe of **1.627**, net of the stated costs (5bps turnover, 50bps borrow, 1-day implementation lag).
4. This cleared my declared `best_so_far_above(1.2)` stop bar on the very first move, so I invoked `stop` — the harness confirmed the rule fired and ended the search there, using only 1 of my 3 allowed content moves.

**Why stop so early:** A single strong feature found on the first candidate scan is about as low-overfitting as this process gets — no multi-feature combination search, no sign-flipping iterations, no swapping. Continuing to add features or search further would have required more moves and risked fitting idiosyncratic in-sample noise for marginal gains, especially since the bar was already cleared comfortably.

**Prediction:** mean OOS Sharpe **0.75**, sd **0.45** — reflecting an expectation of meaningful but not extreme shrinkage from the in-sample 1.627, given the minimal search depth but acknowledging the inherent optimism of picking the best of 80 in-sample candidates and the lack of diversification from using only one feature.
